out_items.name: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting

violations.title: Duty of PIC, Employee Health Policy in Place
violations.observation: Upon discussion with the person-in-charge, one or more of the elements of an effective employee health policy is either missing or incomplete. A complete employee health policy is required to be in place at the food establishment. At the time of this inspection, the Health Department provided and reviewed handouts and resource information in a red folder labeled 'Employee Health Policy.' The CFM had employee health documents for other employees, but not for herself.
violations.corrective_action: The EHS trained the employee and had her complete an employee health policy document during the inspection. CDI

out_items.name: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible

violations.title: Paper Towels Provided
violations.observation: Observed that paper towels were not provided at each handwashing sink. There were no paper towels provided at the handsink behind the front counter.
violations.corrective_action: Provide paper towels at each hand sink to allow employees to properly dry their hands after handwashing. The CFM provided paper towels at the handsink during the inspection.

violations.title: Separation of Raw Animal and RTE Foods
violations.observation: Raw animal food storage, preparation, holding or display conducted in a manner that may cause cross contamination of ready-to-eat food as follows: raw shell eggs were stored over egg nog and milk in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Food shall be protected from cross contamination by separating raw animal foods like poultry, beef, pork, seafood, and eggs from cooked foods, ready-to- eat foods, washed produce, etc during storage, preparation, holding or display. Raw foods shall be stored on shelving units BELOW or SEPARATED from all cooked foods, commercially processed foods, washed produce, leftover foods, etc. The CFM moved the eggs to another lower shelf to correct. CDI.

violations.title: Hot Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed hot holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: the red bean filling in the taiyaki was 108º in the hot holding unit.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature conrol for safety food shall be held hot at a temperature of 135F or above unless the permit holder is using 'time as the public health control' as specified under 3-501.19. Any taiyaki with red bean filling was discarded due to improper hot holding temperature and the establishment not having a time as a public health control agreement on record. Rice Culture (Inspection Date: 12/15/2025) Page 2 of 4

violations.title: Cold Holding
violations.observation: The following food item(s) were observed cold holding at improper temperatures using a calibrated food temperature measuring device: one container of flan and one container of red beans in the Avantco counter top unit in the kitchen were out of cold holding temperature at 44º and 47º, respectively, and in the unit since last Saturday.
violations.corrective_action: Time/temperature control for safety food shall be held cold at a temperature of 41F or below unless the permit holder is using 'time as public health control as specified under section 3-501.19 to limit bacteria growth. The products were discarded. CDI.

violations.title: RTE TCS Food Prepared On Site, Date Marking
violations.observation: The following refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety food that is prepared on site is not used or discarded within 24 hours of preparation and was not observed to be date marked: a large container of red bean paste prepared on site from scratch had a label with a date range of 12/1/25 to 12/15/25.
violations.corrective_action: Refrigerated, ready-to-eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that are prepared on site and kept for more than 24 hours cannot have a shelf-life of more than 7 days, including the day of preparation. These food items must be marked with either the 'consume-by' date and/or 'preparation' date, color-coded labels, or another marking system/method that effectively indicates shelf-life that is clearly understood and properly used by the employees. TCS foods prepared on site can’t have a shelf life of more than 7 days from the day of preparation. If the beans were prepared on 12/1/25, they should have been discarded on 12/6/25. Discard the red beans paste.

out_items.name: Time as a Public Health Control; procedures and records

violations.title: Time as a Public Health Control, Written Procedures
violations.observation: The person in charge is not able to provide written procedures for the use of time as a public health control with the following time/temperature control for safety food item(s): the establishment is using time as a public health control for red bean paste taiyaki filling, but does not have an agreement with the health department to do so.
violations.corrective_action: If time only is used as a public health control for a working supply of time/temperature control for safety food before cooking or for ready to eat, time/temperature control for safety foods that is displayed or held for service for immediate consumption, written procedures shall be prepared in advance and maintained in the food establishment and made available to the regulatory authority upon request. The EHS sent a sample time as a public health control agreement to the manager. Please have it completed by the follow-up, on Tuesday, December 23, 2025.

violations.title: TPHC, Food Marked with 4 Hour End Point
violations.observation: The following food item(s) for which time rather than temperature is used as a control is not marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control: the CFM stated taiyaki with reheated red bean filling was on time as a public health control, but the products in the cabinet which were at 108º were not lableled or marked in any way with an expiration time.
violations.corrective_action: If time only, rather than time in accordance with temperature control, up to a maximum of 4 hours, is used as the public health control the food shall: 1) have an initial temperature of 41F or less if removed from cold holding temperature OR 135F or above if removed from hot holding temperature control, 2) be marked or otherwise identified to indicate the time that is 4 hours past the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, 3) be cooked and served, served if ready-to- eat, or discarded within 4 hours from the point in time when the food is removed from temperature control, and 4) be discarded if unmarked or marked to exceed a 4 hour limit. Before time as a public health control can be used, an agreement must be made with the health department. After the agreement is reached, any foods that are held as TPHC must be marked with an expiration date and time not to exceed 4 hours from when the food was removed from proper holding temperature. Correct by the follow-up.

out_items.name: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used

violations.title: Storage of Poison/Toxic Materials
violations.observation: Observed that poisonous and toxic materials are not properly stored to prevent the contamination of food, equipment, utensils, linens or single service items. A spray bottle of Quick San was stored on a shelf over the food prep area behind the front counter.
violations.corrective_action: All poisonous and toxic materials shall be stored below food, equipment, utensils, linens, and single service items to prevent contamination. The CFM moved the product during the inspection. CDI.

violations.title: In-Use Utensils Proper Storage
violations.observation: Dispensing and/or in-use utensils improperly stored between use as follows: there were large food scoops in the rice and AP flours. The scoop handles were stored in the flours.
violations.corrective_action: During pauses in food preparation or dispensing, food utensils shall be stored in one of the following manners: 1) in the food with their handles above the top of the food and the container, 2) in food that is not time/temperature control for safety (TCS) food with their handles above the top of the food within containers or equipment that can be closed, 3) on a clean portion of the food preparation table or cooking equipment only if the in-use utensil and the food contact surface of the food preparation table or cooking equipment are cleaned and sanitized, 4) in running water of sufficient velocity to flush particulates to the drain, 5) in a clean, protected location if the utensils are used only with a food that is NOT TCS food, or 6) in a container of water if the water is maintained at a temperature of at least 135F and the container is cleaned frequently. Keep scoop handles out of products to prevent unnecessary contact with foods. Correct by the follow-up. Rice Culture (Inspection Date: 12/15/2025) Page 3 of 4

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, Durable/Smooth Materials
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surface of the following equipment is not corrosion resistant, nonabsorbent, and/or smooth: cardboard boxes were being used to line shelving and dunnage racks in the walk-in.
violations.corrective_action: Non-food contact surfaces of equipment that are exposed to splash, spillage, or other foods that require frequent cleaning shall be constructed of a corrosion- resistant, nonabsorbent, and smooth material. Cardboard is not approved for this use. Please remove the cardboard boxes by the follow-up.

violations.title: Food-Contact Surfaces, Durable Materials
violations.observation: The food-contact surfaces of the following equipment and/or utensils are not resistant to corrosion: milk crates were being used to store clean container lids. Milk crates are not approved for storage of food equipment or food.
violations.corrective_action: Materials that are used in the construction of utensils and food-contact surfaces of equipment may not allow the migration of deleterious substances or impart colors, odors, or tastes to food and under normal use conditions shall be resistant to pitting, chipping, crazing, scratching, scoring, distortion, and decomposition. Please remove all milk crates used for storing clean equipment by the follow-up.

violations.title: Nonfood-Contact Surfaces Kept Clean
violations.observation: The nonfood-contact surfaces of the following equipment had accumulations of grime and debris: there was standing water inside the Avantco counter top refrigerator in the kitchen.
violations.corrective_action: Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment and utensils shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil residues. Please clean the standing water out of the unit by the follow-up

violations.title: Jewelry
violations.observation: Employees observed wearing jewelry on their arms and hands while preparing food. A food handler was observed wearing a watch while handling food.
violations.corrective_action: Food employees shall limit their jewelry to a plain wedding ring while preparing food. Food employees may not wear bracelets, watches, etc. because they can inhibit proper hand washing.

out_items.name: Single-use/single-service articles properly stored and used

violations.title: Handled Single-Service/Use Items Storage
violations.observation: Unwrapped plastic spoons were not stored with the handles up, at the self-service countertop .
violations.corrective_action: Knives, forks, and spoons that are not prewrapped shall be presented so that only the handles are touched by employees and consumers if consumer self- service is provided.

out_items.name: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used

violations.title: Equipment, Maintain in Good Repair/Condition
violations.observation: The counter-top cone-filler refrigeration unit is not operating properly and is unable to maintain the fillers at or below 41F.
violations.corrective_action: Repair/adjust the unit so it is able to maintain foods at or below 41F. Do not use the unit to store time/temperature control for safety foods while it is not operating properly. The fillers were relocated to a properly operating refrigerator, during the inspection.

violations.title: Utensils Maintained in Good Repair
violations.observation: The following utensil was observed in a state of repair and condition preventing effective maintenance and cleaning/sanitization: RUBBER SPATULAS. THE SPATULAS WERE WORNOUT AND COULD NOT BE REPAIRED OR PROPERLY CLEANED AND SANITIZED.
violations.corrective_action: Utensils shall be maintained in a state of repair or condition that complies with the requirements specified under Parts 4-1 and 4-2 or shall be discarded. All were discarded during the inspection.
